chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Ahmad b. Hisham al-Mu'addab (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. Ja'far al-Ja'fari narrated to me. He said: I said to Abi'l Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (as):

O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say regarding the Quran, for some among us have disagreed regarding it? One group says it is created, and another group says it is not created. So, he (as) said: I do not say regarding that what they say, but rather I say that it is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.كلام الله: kalam Allah — the word/speech of God, the Imam's preferred designation for the Quran
key_terms.مخلوق: makhluq — created, the Mu'tazilite position that the Quran was created by God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about whether the Quran is created or uncreated?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (as) is asked about the theological debate on whether the Quran is created (makhluq) or uncreated. This question reflects the major Mu'tazilite-Ash'arite controversy that deeply divided early Islamic theology. Rather than siding with either position, the Imam takes a distinct Shia stance: he says the Quran is simply 'the word of Allah' (kalam Allah), avoiding the philosophical categories that both camps employed and grounding the answer in the Quran's divine origin.
